Config drift disabled response caching a.challenged_claim: The r512 config flip of response_cache_enabled to false caused the database overload and latency spike.

counterclaims.statement: The config edit was marked staging-only and not intended for production, so the propagation path that made it effective is unexplained.

evidence_gaps: The cache hit ratio before and after 22:10 is not captured to confirm caching actually stopped.
falsification_tests: Confirm the cache hit ratio dropped to zero at 22:10 and recovered when the flag was re-enabled.

An organic traffic surge overloaded the.challenged_claim: An unrelated organic traffic surge, not the cache flag, overloaded the database.

counterclaims.statement: Response caching was flipped off at 22:10 immediately before read QPS tripled, a direct cause that a surge hypothesis ignores.

evidence_gaps: Edge request volume at 22:10 is not recorded, so a genuine traffic increase cannot be confirmed or excluded.
falsification_tests: Compare edge request volume against database read QPS at 22:10 to see whether load rose independently of the cache flag.

A code change regressed the caching laye.challenged_claim: An application code change regressed the caching layer and disabled caching.

counterclaims.statement: No application deploy accompanied the configuration change, so a code regression is not supported.

evidence_gaps: Deploy and background-job history for the cache service around 22:10 has not been audited.
falsification_tests: Audit deploy and job history for the cache service around 22:10 for any cache-affecting change.
